title: What is a chord?
subtitle: Reading chord charts and your first strum.

scenes.title: What is a chord?
scenes.subtitle: Reading chord charts and your first strum.
lines: In this lesson, you'll learn how to read chord charts and strum your first chord.

scenes.heading: Reading chord charts
lines: A chord is several notes played together by strumming across the strings.
Chord charts show strings as vertical lines, with string 6 on the left, and frets as horizontal lines.
Dots tell you where to place your fingers, numbers show which finger to use, O means an open string, and X means a string you should not play.
Take your time — it all makes sense once you see it in action!

scenes.heading: Your first strum
lines: Your first strum is a smooth, loose motion from the wrist — start at the lowest string of the chord and brush across the others.
Let your thumb or pick glide down, keeping your hand relaxed.
You'll find it feels natural once you move with the motion, not against it.
Take your time — every great guitarist started here.
A chord is a group of notes played together.
Strum from the lowest string with a loose wrist, and keep your hand relaxed.
